predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: Kayin (Karen) State: the claimed Kawthoolei 'comprised the Kayin State and parts of the Mon State, Tanintharyi Region, Bago Region and the Ayeyarwady Division' (2017); only the Kayin State core is…

capitals.name: Papun (Hpapun), capital of the Kawthoolei Free State

ledger.x: 1949: the Karen National Union goes to war on 31 January.
1949: the Karen insurgency begins; the page's claimed Kayin State is the contested zone.
1949-05: the KNU sets up its provisional government at Taungoo.
1950: the Taungoo country passes back to the government.
1953: the KNU 'announced the declaration of the Kawthoolei Free State, based in its capital, Papun'.
1975: Manerplaw is established; 'Manerplaw was established in 1975' and the KNU headquarters is there 'until 1995'.
2024-12-17: the KNU retakes Manerplaw, its headquarters until January 1995.

wars.name: Karen conflict (Internal conflict in Myanmar)
wars.outcome: The KNU lost Manerplaw on 27 January 1995 and signed a ceasefire in January 2012 and the NCA in October 2015.

wars.name: Fall of Manerplaw
wars.outcome: Manerplaw 'captured and occupied' by Tatmadaw and DKBA troops on 27 January 1995 and later abandoned.

wars.name: Post-coup fighting in Karen State
wars.outcome: KNLA claimed Hpapun on 28 March 2024 after a siege from 20 March and the KNU and KNLA recaptured Manerplaw on 17 December 2024; the KNU page gives about 61 percent of Karen State and one third of the Thai border in July 2025.

certainty.note: An insurgent area with no published boundary; Kayin State is a claim, the Manerplaw pocket is the one dated place.
